messages:
julia: hey everyone, first-week question. i triggered the `auth-service` Buildkite pipeline and checkout failed with 403 saying 'Repository not found'. i accepted the org invite but used my personal github account a while back — could that be the issue?

nik: welcome Julia :wave: possible. if the invite went to your work email but you accepted it on a different GH account, the org membership won't line up with the CI GH App. can you paste the short checkout log?

julia: clipped log: `fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/redwood/auth-service.git/': The requested URL returned error: 403\nremote: Repository not found.`

ash: two quick checks: 1) github.com/orgs/redwood/people — search for your username/email, 2) check your primary verified email on GitHub (Settings -> Emails) to ensure it matches the invite. if SSO/SCIM provisioned you might have a different github username created for your SSO identity.

julia: i see two accounts tied to my work email (one old personal acct with the same email and a new SSO account). the org shows the SSO account as member but the Buildkite job log shows the git clone attempted with a token belonging to my old account login.

nik: that explains it. the GH App installation maps to the org membership & team. if the CI job got a credential from the wrong linked account (rare, but can happen when you accept invites across multiple accounts), the clone will be rejected. i'll re-invite the SSO account and remove the stale account access.

infra-bot: infra:created ticket #2899 "Resolve julia github account mismatch / ensure correct org membership for CI" (assignee: nik)

ash: also check if your GitHub primary email is verified. Unverified emails can cause access issues for org apps. we had one onboarding case where the user accepted the invite but didn't verify the email and GH blocked app installs.

julia: verified emails now and removed the old personal account from the invite. accepted the org invite on the SSO account. i added my SSH pubkey too.

buildkite-bot: Buildkite: pipeline `auth-service/push` #71 failed on job `checkout` \u2014 exit code 128 \u2014 fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address

nik: hm it still hit HTTPS in the agent. did you push any branches upstream or are you testing from a fork? also check `git remote -v` and confirm no https remotes in the repo config.

julia: repo is a direct branch on upstream, remote shows `git@github.com:redwood/auth-service.git` locally. i think the agent is configured to use a deploy key for clones; maybe the repo-level GH App install hasn't been granted yet.

ash: right — sometimes CI runners use a deploy key or the org GH App depending on agent pool. i've re-requested the GH App install for `auth-service` and re-sent the team invite to `ci-core`. give it a minute.

infra-bot: infra:action taken "re-request GH App install for auth-service" and assigned #2899 to nik

nik: invited you to `ci-core` and re-requested app install. once you accept, re-run the pipeline. i also flipped the checkout hook to prefer SSH remotes for the agent pool handling `auth-service` so it won't fall back to https.

julia: accepted `ci-core` and re-approved GH App install. re-triggered the Buildkite run.

buildkite-bot: Buildkite: pipeline `auth-service/push` #72 succeeded on job `checkout` \u2014 duration 37s

ash: awesome. root cause summary for onboarding doc: account/email mismatch (SSO vs old personal account) + unverified email prevented proper app mapping, and pipeline agent fallback to HTTPS. checklist item: verify primary email, confirm SSO account, add SSH key, join `ci-core`, and accept GH App install.

julia: thanks all for the help and fast turnaround! i'll add a short note to the onboarding doc about verifying the correct GitHub account after SSO provisioning.

nik: closing infra ticket #2899. welcome aboard :tada:

buildkite-bot: Buildkite: pipeline `auth-service/push` #73 started build steps after checkout
